newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: NatSteel Broadway placement taken - DBS.
newsitem.headline: NatSteel Broadway placement taken - DBS.

text.p: Half the 33.8 million shares NatSteel Broadway Ltd is offering at US$0.70 each in an initial public offer (IPO) have been taken in a placement, DBS Bank, said on Thursday.
Bank executive vice president Eric Ang, speaking at the launch of the Hong Kong-based contract manufacturing company's IPO, said DBS was in charge of the placement portion of the issue.
He said the remaining 16.9 million shares to be offered to the public would be taken care of by Overseas Union Bank. DBS and OUB are joint lead managers and underwriters of the issue.

Ang, head of investment banking for DBS, said he was sure the U.S. dollar issue would be a success, despite a lacklustre stock market, because it was being priced at a discount to the market compared with other contract manufacturers.
NatSteel Broadway shares are being offered at a price earnings ratio of 9.2 times its forecast 1996 earnings.
The company has forecast pretax profits of HK$68.4 million on turnover of HK$521.0 million for the year ending December 1996.
The company, a spin-off of NatSteel Ltd, plans to use estimated net proceeds of US$22.36 million mainly to expand production facilities and reduce bank borrowings.

Ang also said the company would not be affected by the current slump in electronics as it was involved mainly in the consumer electronics sector and not the information technology sector, which is experiencing the slow growth.
The fact that all of NatSteel Broadway's plants were in China was also a plus factor because of the lower cost of labour there, he said.
NatSteel president Ang Kong Hua said the group decided to list NatSteel Broadway in Singapore instead of Hong Kong because there was better recognition of the "NatSteel" name among investors here.
